content.takeaway: Config change caused outage; alert and status page were slow; config review and faster alerts agreed.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § step#1
Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § text#0

content.markdown: At 16:40, a config change to the payments service was deployed. It incorrectly set the gateway connection pool from 50 to 5 connections, instead of the intended 55.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § step#2
Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § text#1

content.markdown: Checkout requests began queuing for connections and timing out almost immediately due to the reduced connection pool.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § step#3
Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § text#2

content.markdown:
The error-rate alert fired at 17:02, 22 minutes after the config change. The alert is configured to fire when the checkout error rate is above 10% for 15 minutes. Errors exceeded 10% around 16:47, so 17:02 was the earliest it could fire.

**From the source:** 02

**From the source:** 02

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § step#4
Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § text#3

content.markdown: The faulty config was rolled back at 17:15.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § step#5
Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § text#4

content.markdown: Checkout was fully recovered at 17:27. Customers experienced errors for a total of 47 minutes, resulting in approximately 2,300 failed checkouts and 140 support tickets before the status page was updated.

nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § step#6
Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § text#5

content.markdown: The status page was updated at 17:20, 40 minutes after errors began. This was delayed because the incident commander (Marcus) was busy with the rollback and it was not his priority.

nodes.title: Alert threshold too slow
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § problem#1

content.markdown: The current alert threshold of 10% over 15 minutes is too slow for checkout, leading to significant lost revenue.

nodes.title: New alert threshold agreed
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § solution#1

content.markdown:
The checkout error-rate alert will be lowered to 5% over 5 minutes. This change is owned by Marcus and will be implemented by Wednesday, March 19. This new threshold would have triggered two noisy pages in the last 30 days, both during payment provider maintenance, which is acceptable.

**From the source:** twice

nodes.title: Support can post status page directly
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § solution#2

content.markdown: Support will be allowed to post status-page updates directly, without waiting for the incident commander.

nodes.title: No review for config changes
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § problem#2

content.markdown: Config changes for payments do not undergo code review. They are edited and applied directly via the deploy dashboard, unlike code changes which require two approvals.

nodes.title: Config review gap
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § part 1 § problem#3

content.markdown: This lack of review is a significant gap, as a typo in code would likely be caught by a reviewer or tests.

nodes.title: Cause and Effect
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#0

content.markdown: A typo in a config change (50 to 5 connections) directly caused checkout requests to queue and timeout. This highlights a critical vulnerability in the deployment process for configuration changes.

nodes.title: Detection Delay
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#1

content.markdown: The error-rate alert fired 22 minutes after the config change, due to a 15-minute threshold. This delay meant customers experienced errors for a significant period before the incident was formally detected.

nodes.title: Recovery Time
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#2

content.markdown: Once the alert fired, rollback and full recovery took 25 minutes. The total customer impact was 47 minutes, with 2,300 failed checkouts.

nodes.title: Process Gaps Identified
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#3

content.markdown: The review identified three key process gaps: slow alert thresholds, delayed status page updates, and a lack of review for config changes.

nodes.title: Agreed Actions
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#4

content.markdown: Actions agreed upon include lowering the checkout error-rate alert to 5% over 5 minutes, allowing support to directly update the status page, and implementing pull-request review for payments service config changes.

nodes.title: Open Questions/Deferred Decisions
nodes.stableKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#5

content.markdown: Decisions on a Friday deploy freeze and automatic rollback are deferred, pending further analysis. The status of customer retries for failed checkouts is also an open question.
